resume.title: Resume
resume.subtitle: AI Platform Engineer · Buenos Aires
resume.summary: Platform engineer, 10+ years shipping software. For the last two years I have been building Imperia OS — a runtime where an LLM call is an atomic state-machine step, not a wrapper around an API: agents, tools over MCP, three knowledge stores (code graph, documents, relational data) and a dev → standby → prod deploy pipeline. In production since 2025, written solo. Before that: blockchain infrastructure at Sber, IBM and Insolar, and cross-platform products on Flutter/AWS. I am not interested in "adding AI" to a product — I am interested in systems where the model is part of the runtime.

bullets: State-machine runtime: an LLM call is an atomic step with typed input and output, not a free-running chat loop. Every agent turn is reproducible and inspectable step by step.
MCP tool layer: ~90 tools (data, git, browser, deploy, messengers) behind one protocol, with access partitioned into registers by how reversible the action is.

Three knowledge stores behind one access path: code and architecture graph (Kuzu), documents and vector memory (MongoDB), relational data (PostgreSQL) — each owned by its own service, never connected to directly from agent code.
Agent orchestration: topic-parallel turns, delegation to background workers, judge panels that adversarially verify findings, A/B runs scored by an LLM judge.
dev → standby → prod deploy pipeline with gates, auto-promotion and single-commit rollback; the coordinator holds the only path to production.
Input collectors: Telegram (MTProto), WhatsApp, voice with transcription and per-word confidence — all folded into a single event stream.
Cross-platform mobile platform on Flutter + AWS, brought to a high level of functional readiness.
Clean Architecture from day one; feature-based modularity on the front end, event-driven reactive architecture (BLoC → Cubit → Riverpod).
Infrastructure as Code with AWS CDK: reproducible environments and automated deployment.
Backend: Amplify/Cognito auth, business logic on Lambda (Go), DynamoDB with composite keys, media in S3.
Sber: CRUD abstraction layer over Hyperledger Fabric — feature implementation time from ~8 hours to ~15 minutes. Self-initiated and delivered after hours.

IBM: full test environment and CI/CD for Hyperledger Fabric — doubled delivery speed; refactored project structure (−30% codebase); led a CouchDB → LevelDB migration (+40% data operation performance); shipped cross-channel encryption with zero defects despite no formal requirements.
Insolar: data architecture for a blockchain wallet; guided a newly onboarded system architect through the key design decisions.
Bancor: replaced Hyperledger Fabric usage with Bitcoin-based anchoring.
ShelterZoom: identified flaws in their Fabric setup and proposed a simpler, faster immutable-store design.
Implemented Diasoft Flextera front-office, reporting modules and business-process debugging; back-office system and Oracle DB.
Java/JavaScript data handlers, state-machine configuration and access-rights management.
Custom form builder (Ruby on Rails) for contractor work tracking — dynamic data objects on top of a relational database.
Cross-platform native client (Codename One, Java, SQLite): text, numbers, photos, map markers, camera and geolocation capture.
Offline support with automatic sync; server side in Java/MySQL/javax.servlet. Delivered a working MVP.
Android app with local SQLite and sync through a server (MySQL, Tomcat, Jersey, Jsch), plus a photo-capture module with SSH upload.
Reworked the architecture per client request to send data directly from the app.
Programmed an STM32F4Discovery board as the bridge between a PC and a spectrograph controller.
Independently built the spectrograph software for qualitative and quantitative materials analysis; multithreading for three spectrometers at once; full technical documentation.

imperiaOs.title: Imperia OS
imperiaOs.subtitle: AI-first development platform. Shipped and running since 2025.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.text: AI assistants today are stateless — no memory between sessions, no understanding of your business, no ability to act on real systems. Each interaction starts from zero. Building a real assistant requires a platform: runtime, knowledge, infrastructure.

solution.title: Architecture
solution.text: State-machine runtime where LLMs are atomic steps. Three knowledge graphs — business model, test scenarios, code structure. Agent system that reads all three and acts. Infrastructure that deploys and monitors itself.

steps: Business scenarios defined in the knowledge graph
Agents read the graph, write code, deploy — same pipeline for everything
imperiaOs.caseStudyTeaser: Imperia OS is also written up as a case study — architecture, decisions and what they cost.

imperia-os.title: Imperia OS — AI-First Development Platform
imperia-os.description: Full-stack AI platform with state-machine runtime, three knowledge graphs, and self-building agent system.
imperia-os.problem: AI assistants are stateless — no persistent memory, no business context, no ability to act on real systems. Building a real assistant requires a platform: runtime, knowledge base, agent system, and infrastructure.
imperia-os.solution: Built Imperia OS from scratch: state-machine runtime where LLMs are atomic steps, three knowledge graphs (business model, tests, code), MCP tool system for typed database access, and hot-standby infrastructure with automatic failover.
technicalDetails: State-machine runtime for deterministic LLM orchestration
Three knowledge graphs in Kuzu: business domain, tests, code structure
MCP tool system — PostgreSQL, Kuzu, MongoDB via typed interfaces
Thought engine — persistent memory with wikilinks and embeddings
Hot standby with 15s health checks and automatic failover
results: Development flow: business scenarios → tests → agents generate code
lessonsLearned: LLMs become reliable when each call is a bounded step in a state machine
Three separate knowledge graphs beat one merged graph — different query patterns need different schemas
Building the platform with itself is the strongest validation

mobile-platform.title: Cross-Platform Mobile Platform
mobile-platform.description: Scalable mobile platform on Flutter and AWS with clean architecture and automated infrastructure.
mobile-platform.problem: Needed a foundation for a cross-platform product with reliable backend and automated deployment. Typical approaches led to fragmented architecture.
mobile-platform.solution: Implemented Clean Architecture with Feature-based structure in Flutter. Backend - serverless on AWS (Lambda in Golang). Infrastructure defined in CDK and deploys automatically.
technicalDetails: Serverless backend on AWS (Lambda, DynamoDB, Cognito)
lessonsLearned: Clean Architecture pays off on large projects
Infrastructure as Code is critical for reproducibility

website-builder.title: Dynamic Website Builder Platform
website-builder.description: Flexible website builder system with dynamic data schema and multi-tenancy support.
website-builder.problem: Needed a builder where users can create arbitrary entity types and fields without DB migrations. Plus data isolation between clients.
website-builder.solution: Implemented EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) pattern with multi-tenancy at the database level. Users create their entities and fields through the interface, data is stored in a universal and extensible structure.
technicalDetails: EAV pattern for dynamic schema without migrations
Multi-tenancy with isolated databases per client
Type-safe storage of different data types
results: Users create entities without developer involvement
System adapts to different business domains
lessonsLearned: EAV provides maximum flexibility but requires query optimization
Multi-tenancy at DB level is the most reliable isolation
